question: What public callback metadata contract should generic Telegram agent turns receive for inline-button clicks?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the safe fix is not a one-line id swap because callback query id and source message id serve different contracts for dedupe, answering, editing, and agent-visible metadata.

options.title: Expose separate source-message metadata
options.body: Preserve callback query id for event identity while adding source chat/message ids to agent metadata and current-message tool context; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Keep generic callbacks text-only
options.body: Document that only plugin interactive callbacks can edit the originating message and close this gap as unsupported generic-agent behavior.

options.title: Plugin-only handoff
options.body: Require inline-button workflows that edit the originating message to use registered plugin interactive handlers, leaving generic `callback_data` fallback unchanged.

recommendation.title: Expose separate source-message metadata
recommendation.body: Preserve callback query id for event identity while adding source chat/message ids to agent metadata and current-message tool context; this is the recommended path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing owner from recent shared channel/plugin runtime history and current maintainer context for deciding cross-agent metadata contracts.
